records.label: spacr.qt.mask_engine.secondary_object_instances#1
records.source: Every positive primary label is a marker, including all its pixels. Intensity growth follows the negative, optionally Gaussian-smoothed image. Distance growth floods a flat surface from the primary pixels. Common stop thresholds constrain four-connected paths around excluded pixels; seed_fraction trims after growth. This is not unrestricted Euclidean nearest-primary assignment. Neither mode is CellProfiler's distance/intensity Propagation algorithm.
records.context: Every positive primary label is a marker, including all its pixels. Intensity growth follows the negative, optionally Gaussian-smoothed image. Distance growth floods a flat surface from the primary pixels. Common stop thresholds constrain four-connected paths around excluded pixels; seed_fraction trims after growth. This is not unrestricted Euclidean nearest-primary assignment. Neither mode is CellProfiler's distance/intensity Propagation algorithm.
records.translation: Cada etiqueta primaria positiva es un marcador, incluidos todos sus píxeles. El crecimiento por intensidad sigue la imagen en negativo, opcionalmente suavizada con una gaussiana. El crecimiento por distancia inunda una superficie plana desde los píxeles primarios. Los umbrales de parada comunes restringen los caminos de conectividad a cuatro vecinos alrededor de los píxeles excluidos; seed_fraction recorta después del crecimiento. Esto no es una asignación sin restricciones al primario euclidiano más cercano. Ninguno de los dos modos es el algoritmo de propagación distancia/intensidad (Propagation) de CellProfiler.
records.review_basis: MT draft edited in AI review

records.label: spacr.qt.mask_engine.secondary_object_instances#2
records.source: The four rules in :data:`PROPAGATE_STOPS` use processed intensities. ``absolute``, ``percentile`` and ``threshold`` restrict growth with a common foreground mask. ``seed_fraction`` trims each watershed basin at a fraction of the brightest processed pixel inside its primary. That ratio is not a quantile and depends on background offset. With a dark nucleus in a cytoplasmic channel, use a common threshold instead of a nucleus-relative peak ratio.
records.context: The four rules in :data:`PROPAGATE_STOPS` use processed intensities. ``absolute``, ``percentile`` and ``threshold`` restrict growth with a common foreground mask. ``seed_fraction`` trims each watershed basin at a fraction of the brightest processed pixel inside its primary. That ratio is not a quantile and depends on background offset. With a dark nucleus in a cytoplasmic image data channel, use a common threshold instead of a nucleus-relative peak ratio.
records.translation: Las cuatro reglas de :data:`PROPAGATE_STOPS` usan intensidades procesadas. ``absolute``, ``percentile`` y ``threshold`` restringen el crecimiento con una máscara de primer plano común. ``seed_fraction`` recorta cada cuenca del watershed a una fracción del píxel procesado más brillante dentro de su primario. Esa razón no es un cuantil y depende del desplazamiento de fondo. Con un núcleo oscuro en un canal citoplasmático, use un umbral común en lugar de una proporción respecto al pico del núcleo.
records.review_basis: MT draft edited in AI review

records.label: spacr.qt.mask_engine.secondary_object_instances#3
records.source: Primary pixels are always included before minimum-area filtering, even below the threshold. Hole filling can also restore below-threshold pixels. Filtering can remove a whole secondary together with its seed; the missing ID is reported. Remaining labels retain their primary IDs exactly, without splitting or renumbering disconnected components. Sparse IDs use compact internal markers, never arrays sized by max ID.
records.context: Primary pixels are always included before minimum-area filtering, even below the threshold. Hole filling can also restore below-threshold pixels. Filtering can remove a whole secondary together with its seed; the missing ID is reported. Remaining labels retain their primary IDs exactly, without splitting or renumbering disconnected components. Sparse IDs use compact internal markers, never arrays sized by max ID.
records.translation: Los píxeles primarios se incluyen siempre antes del filtrado por área mínima, incluso por debajo del umbral. El relleno de huecos también puede restaurar píxeles por debajo del umbral. El filtrado puede eliminar un secundario completo junto con su semilla; el ID ausente se notifica. Las etiquetas restantes conservan exactamente sus ID primarios, sin separar ni renumerar componentes desconectados. Los ID dispersos usan marcadores internos compactos, nunca matrices dimensionadas por el ID máximo.
records.review_basis: MT draft edited in AI review

records.context: A pixel is on an outline when it belongs to an object and one of its four neighbours does not belong to the same one. ``like`` is the entry the bundle had: an entry holding only 0 and 1 gets a 0/1 outline back, and one holding ids gets each outline pixel's id, which is what Cellpose's own ``masks_flows_to_seg`` writes. An entry of all zeros says nothing about its form and gets ids, Cellpose's default.
records.translation: Un píxel está en un contorno cuando pertenece a un objeto y uno de sus cuatro vecinos no pertenece al mismo. ``like`` es la entrada que tenía el paquete: una entrada que solo contiene 0 y 1 recibe un contorno 0/1, y una que contiene id recibe el id de cada píxel del contorno, que es lo que escribe el propio ``masks_flows_to_seg`` de Cellpose. records.label: spacr.qt.mask_engine.shrink_objects#1
records.source: Each object is eroded against everything that is not itself -- background AND the objects touching it -- so two objects sharing a border both pull back from it and the seam between them widens. Eroding the foreground as one binary would instead leave that seam untouched, which is the opposite of what a curator reaching for Shrink wants.
records.context: Each object is eroded against everything that is not itself -- background AND the objects touching it -- so two objects sharing a border both pull back from it and the seam between them widens. Eroding the foreground as one binary would instead leave that seam untouched, which is the opposite of what a curator reaching for Shrink wants.
records.translation: Cada objeto se erosiona frente a todo lo que no es él mismo -- el fondo Y los objetos que lo tocan --, de modo que dos objetos que comparten un borde se retiran ambos de él y la costura entre ellos se ensancha. Erosionar el primer plano como un único binario dejaría en cambio esa costura intacta, que es lo contrario de lo que quiere un curador que recurre a Shrink.
records.review_basis: MT draft edited in AI review
